Let's re-read carefully: "Thus queens in consecutive rows cannot occupy columns differing by 1." This confirms the "no touching" rule applies to adjacent cells (orthogonal and diagonal). It also clarifies that long diagonals are allowed ("Queens separated by more than one row MAY share a long diagonal"). So, it's not the standard N-Queens problem where *any* two queens on a diagonal attack each other. It's a "no-touching" constraint (like placing kings so they don't attack), plus the regional constraint.
